To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

maternal and embryonically expressed sid-1 are independently required for parental RNA interference in C. elegans, that maternal rme2 is not absolutely required, and that dsRNA can be taken into cells by endocytosis independent of sid-1.

maternal dsRNA can reach embryos by multiple paths that include sid-1-dependent and -independent routes, and that maternal dsRNA is transported through the RAB7 endocytotic pathway independently of sid activity.
parental RNA interference in Caenorhabdits elegans requires the SID-1 dsRNA transporter, SID-5, and RME-2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the mechanisms of RNA interference in C. elegans.
the inheritance of RNAi.
understanding the mechanisms by which dsRNA is trafficked between cells in C. elegans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
parental RNAi is complex and involves multiple pathways, but sid-1 is the only gene absolutely required.
sid-1, but not sid genes 2, 3, or 5, or rme-2, is required for parental RNA interference.

the inheritance of silencing by RNAi in C. elegans requires the following: (i) maternal sid-1 and maternal dsRNA, which are transported into oocytes and embryos; (ii) maternal dsRNA that is taken up directly by the embryos; and (iii) maternal dsRNA in the yolk, which is taken up by embryos.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
maternal sid-1 and rme-3, and embryonic sid5 are required for parental RNAI, and sid-3, sid-5, and rme-4 contribute to but are not required for parental silencing.   2
parental RNAi is complex and involves multiple paths for maternal dsRNAs to reach embryos and multiple mechanisms for maternal dsRNas to enter the RNAi pathway.
maternal sid-1 is required to initiate parental RNAi, maternal sid-5 and rme-1 are required to maintain parental RNAi, and maternal rme-1 and rme-4 are required for the inheritance of dsRNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is more than one path for dsRNA to reach progeny and initiate RNAi, and the relative contributions of the different pathways are tissue specific.
the mechanisms that underlie parental RNAi in Caenrohabditis elegan are more complex and diverse than previously thought.
the mechanisms of RNAi inheritance are complex, and that multiple independent paths exist to support inheritance of silencing signals.
